newsitem.title: UK: OPEC crude output rises to 26.9 mln bpd in Jan - IEA.
newsitem.headline: OPEC crude output rises to 26.9 mln bpd in Jan - IEA.

text.p: Crude oil production by members of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) rose to 26.9 million barrels per day (bpd) in January from December's 26.6 million bpd, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
The figure was well above OPEC's self-assigned but long-ignored production ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.

A 240,000 bpd increase in Iraqi output in January, the first full month of exports since Baghdad returned to the oil market in December after a six-year absence, accounted for most of the gains, the IEA said in its latest monthly report.

"OPEC production increased sharply again in January as Iraq exported about 550,000 bpd under the U.N. oil-for-food programme, about 240,000 bpd more than the average achieved in December since the programme did not begin until part way through the month," the Paris-based agency said.
OPEC heavyweights Saudi Arabia and Iran saw little change in their output in January but both continued to produce in excess of their quotas, the IEA said.
But several other members outside the Gulf produced more in January, particularly in Nigeria and Venezuela, seen by the IEA and other observers as OPEC's biggest quota violator.

"The largest OPEC increase outside of the Persian Gulf occurred in Nigeria, where production rose by about 45,000 bpd," the IEA said, pointing to escalating production from the new offshore Ngo field and increased output in the Qua Iboe area.
Venezuelan production is estimated to have risen by a similar amount to almost 3.1 million bpd, against its OPEC quota of 2.359 million.
